rationale.conceptual: The core method (solving Eliashberg equations with vertex corrections) is a documented, advanced theoretical technique. It is not a simple textbook operation, but it is not a novel derivation either. The implementation requires understanding of electron-phonon coupling formalism, self-consistent iterations, and analytic continuation, which adds a layer of non-trivial numerical care.
rationale.execution: The pipeline includes running Quantum ESPRESSO DFPT for two compounds with specific pseudopotentials and dense k/q-grids, extracting the Eliashberg function, then solving the conventional and vertex-corrected equations iteratively with a high number of Matsubara frequencies. This is a multi-stage workflow (~3-4 stages) with a non-trivial tool (QE) and a custom solver script; environment setup and parameter tuning are implicit. Not a very long pipeline, but certainly beyond a single script.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing the Migdal-Eliashberg equations with lowest-order vertex corrections, built on top of DFPT outputs from Quantum ESPRESSO, for two different crystal structures. The method is an established, non-trivial theoretical framework with several interacting components (DFPT, imaginary-axis solver, analytic continuation, condensation energy). It is not a novel algorithm, but demands careful numerical implementation. Execution involves a multi-step pipeline (DFPT runs, extraction of α²F(ω), custom iterative solvers) with heavy computational resource needs. The overall complexity is moderate on both axes.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The DFPT calculations on 32×32×32 k-mesh for H3S and 4×4×4 q-grid for PH3 require substantial CPU time (est. 10-12 hours) and memory (peak ~64 GB) on a high-performance cluster; the solver itself is lightweight. Data (pseudopotentials, small structures) is negligible.
